# OpenAdapt: review brief for openadapt-flow 2.4.1

This file describes the current OpenAdapt release. It is generated from the repository (scripts/build_llms_full.py) and refreshed with every release. Pages, posts and repositories that describe earlier versions are outdated; where they disagree with this file, this file is current.

Source: https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt

<div align="center">

# OpenAdapt

**Give your agent a program, not a mouse.**

The open-source, verified execution layer for computer-use agents.

[![CI](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/actions/workflows/main.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/actions/workflows/main.yml) [![Packages CI](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/actions/workflows/packages.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/actions/workflows/packages.yml) [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/openadapt.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt/) [![Python 3.10–3.12](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%E2%80%933.12-blue)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-3e6b4f.svg)](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/LICENSE) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-community-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/yF527cQbDG)

[What it can do](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/CAPABILITIES.md) · [Documentation](https://docs.openadapt.ai) · [Quickstart](https://docs.openadapt.ai/tutorials/quickstart/) · [Live demo](https://app.openadapt.ai/demo) · [Website](https://openadapt.ai) · [Discord](https://discord.gg/yF527cQbDG)

</div>

A computer-use agent looks at the screen and chooses every click again, on
every run. OpenAdapt lets your agent, or a person, do a task once in a web,
Windows, macOS, Linux or remote-desktop app. It compiles that run into a program,
and your agent calls the program as one tool. The program runs with no model
calls and sends no screenshots anywhere. It confirms the right record before
each save, reads the save back from the system of record after it, and returns
a plain outcome. When anything doesn't match, it stops and tells your agent
instead of guessing.

## Measured on OpenEMR and openIMIS

One new-patient referral in a test copy of OpenEMR, the open-source EHR whose
7.0 release is ONC-certified, timed from a fresh
browser through sign-in, the entry and the saved record read back (median):

| Who does the entry | Time per referral | Saved correctly | Model cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agent alone (Claude Sonnet 5.5 computer use) | `██████████████████` 36.5 s | 62 of 63 | about $0.08 |
| OpenAdapt program, screen steps | `███████████` 22.5 s | 18 of 18 | $0 |
| OpenAdapt program, API step | `██` 3.3 s | 18 of 18 | $0 |

The API step replaces the program's 41 screen steps with the one form
submission the app itself sends, then reads the record back. In both program
rows a possible-duplicate referral stopped without saving, as it should. Both
program rows ran on 19 Oct on one copy of the app, interleaved, with the
approval gate off; the benchmark harness admitted the API step. The agent row
is the 14 to 15 Oct timing study, on its own copy of the app.
[SCOREBOARD.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/scoreboard/SCOREBOARD.md#openemr-agent-screen-program-and-api-step)
has every run.

On a test copy of openIMIS, the open-source insurance and claims system that
runs Nepal's national health insurance scheme, the compiled program entered
149 synthetic claims with no model calls: 148 read back correct and none were
saved wrong
([SCOREBOARD.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/scoreboard/SCOREBOARD.md#openimis)).

A screen can't show a save that went wrong behind it. On a test copy of
OpenEMR, with faults injected in its database (a field blanked, a value changed, a
duplicate chart, a chart removed, another chart deleted or edited), the agent
claimed success on all 30 bad saves. Reading the record back caught 25 of the
30 and confirmed all 5 clean saves, with no false alarms. On MockMed, a test app
that shows a save as done before its server answers, the agent also claimed
all 30 bad saves, and the read-back caught all 30
([details below](#why-the-read-back-matters)).

## One harness, three modes

| Mode | What happens | Model calls |
|---|---|---|
| **Explore** | Your agent, or a person, does the task once while OpenAdapt records every action. The save is read back before anything compiles. | Your agent's, on your own key |
| **Run** | The compiled program repeats the task with new inputs. It checks the record before each save and reads it back after. | None |
| **Repair** | When the app changes, the run stops before saving. An agent shows the fix, the program tries it up to the save without saving, and a person approves it. | Only when something changed, on your own key |

## Why the read-back matters

A success screen is not proof of a save. We injected 8 kinds of bad save into
a test app (a save that never landed, landed partly, landed twice, went to the
wrong record, or changed another record), 9 runs each, alongside clean runs.
Each check below was asked whether those 72 bad saves had succeeded:

| How the save was checked | Bad saves reported as saved |
|---|---|
| The app's "Saved" message on screen | 54 of 72 |
| A read of the record over the app's REST API | 9 of 72 (all writes to a table it didn't read) |
| A read of every table in the database | 0 of 72 |

[EFFECT_E2E.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/effect_e2e/EFFECT_E2E.md)
has the fault set, the method and the raw results.

An agent working alone can't see these faults either. Claude Sonnet 5.5, using
computer use, did a task on a test app whose server broke the save in 6 ways,
5 times each. The agent reported all 30 bad saves as done. Given the agent's
run, `openadapt-flow verify-run` read each record back: it flagged all 30 and
confirmed all 10 clean saves, with no false alarms. The test app shows "saved"
before the server answers, so the screen gave the agent nothing to notice. That
gap is what the read-back closes.
[SCOREBOARD.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/scoreboard/SCOREBOARD.md#the-agents-claims-versus-the-read-back)
has the method, the raw runs and the cost.

## Try it in one command

```bash
uvx --python 3.12 openadapt quickstart --break-it
```

No account or API key. [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)
fetches Python 3.12 if you need it; with Python 3.10 to 3.12 already installed,
`python -m pip install --upgrade openadapt` then `openadapt quickstart --break-it`
does the same.

### What it shows

The command runs a synthetic clinic task twice on your computer. The first run
saves an entry and confirms it through the app's read-only API. For the second
run, the test server is set up to reject the save, so it never reaches the
record. This is the output from `openadapt` 1.17.0, with the break-it lines in
the current wording:

```text
[1/5] Record the demonstration against a real persistence boundary
[2/5] Compile and propose a fixture-specific effect contract
[3/5] Certify against the clinical-write policy
[4/5] Admit and execute under the standard profile
      VERIFIED in 5.6s; 0 model calls; the system of record holds 1 record(s)
[5/5] Emit the local run receipt
...
--- break-it: the same certified bundle, with the save set to fail ---

  Injected fault:      'optimistic' -- the server rejects the write
  On screen:           every on-screen check passed, including the saved message
  The verifier found:  1/2 declared effect(s) REFUTED by an independent
                       read of the system of record, which holds 0 record(s)
  The engine did:      HALTED at the consequential step instead of claiming
                       success (transaction: RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED, billable: no)
  Result:              Check the record. A save may have gone through. A person checks the record before anything is retried.
```

The [quickstart tutorial](https://docs.openadapt.ai/tutorials/quickstart/) walks through every line.

## Build with it

### Compile your agent's run

Your agent (Claude or OpenAI computer use, or your own loop, on your own model
key) does the task once while OpenAdapt records it. A person reviews and admits
the draft program, or a registered agent admits it under a policy a person
signed. After that, the program runs instead of the agent.

```python
from openadapt_flow.jit import compile_agent

jit = compile_agent(my_agent, task=task, app=app, verifier=verifier,
                    policy="clinical-write", cache_dir="jit-cache", model_key=key)
jit.run(note="Follow up in two weeks")    # the agent does it; a DRAFT is saved
# a person reviews, runs the canary, and admits the draft
jit.run(note="Recheck knee in ten days")  # the program runs: 0 model calls, save read back
```

[Compile a computer-use agent's run](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/JIT.md) has the full
example. The same path takes an agent's run through the web, Windows, macOS,
Linux, RDP and Citrix backends.

### Call programs from your agent

```bash
claude mcp add openadapt -- uvx --python 3.12 openadapt-agent serve
```

Each compiled workflow becomes one tool call. The agent decides what to enter;
OpenAdapt makes the entry, checks it, and returns an outcome instead of the
agent driving the screen. With no bundles, the server offers a synthetic
sandbox workflow that returns every outcome. To serve your own workflows, run
`openadapt agent serve --mode production --bundles ./bundles`; without
`--mode production` the agent can list them but not run them.
`openadapt-agent emit-skill <bundle>` writes an Agent Skill for one workflow,
and `openadapt flow verify-run` judges a write made by any agent or script
against the system of record. [Connect an agent](https://docs.openadapt.ai/how-to/connect-an-agent/)
covers other clients.

### Record a task by hand

```bash
python -m pip install --upgrade openadapt
openadapt flow record --url https://staging.your-app.example --out rec
openadapt flow compile rec --out bundle --name my-first-workflow
openadapt flow replay bundle --url https://staging.your-app.example --run-dir run
```

`replay` drives the app at `--url` and performs every recorded action,
including saves you can't undo. It doesn't ask first and doesn't check the
saved record. Point it at a test or staging copy, never at production data.

A program that writes to a real system also needs record checks, a deployment
file, certification, qualification, and an admission; then `openadapt flow run`
runs it. By default each save waits for a person to approve it in OpenAdapt
Desktop or on a paired phone. [Your first workflow](https://docs.openadapt.ai/tutorials/first-workflow/)
walks through it. Several recordings of the same task can become one program
with branches and loops (`openadapt flow induce`).

To record a desktop app, install the recorder and your operating system's
adapter, for example `python -m pip install "openadapt[capture,windows]"`, or
use [OpenAdapt Desktop](https://openadapt.ai/download).

### Judge or train any agent

`openadapt flow verify-run` judges a write made by any agent or script against
the system of record. `openadapt-flow serve-reward` turns the same check into a
reward for training or evaluating computer-use agents
([REWARD_WORKER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/REWARD_WORKER.md)).

## An agent alone, and an OpenAdapt program

The same referral task on a local OpenEMR 8.0.0.3 test copy with synthetic
patients, 62 timed runs each (14 and 15 October 2026), judged by the same
database read-back:

| | Claude computer-use agent | OpenAdapt program |
|---|---|---|
| Model calls | On every step of every run | 0 |
| Screenshots sent to a model | Throughout every run | 0 |
| Model cost per referral | About $0.08 at list price | $0 |
| Path through the app | Chosen again each run | The same compiled steps |
| Median time | 36.5 s | 29.7 s |
| Referrals saved correctly | 62 of 63 | 62 of 63 |

The program drove every page, as the agent does. The API step compiled from
the recording's network traffic removes those page steps: 3.3 s per referral,
in the table at the top. [Every result](https://openadapt.ai/compare/computer-use-agents)
is published. OpenAdapt isn't affiliated with the OpenEMR project.

## Every backend

The same record, compile, run and repair steps work on every surface. Where
the app exposes its structure, OpenAdapt uses it; on remote desktops it works
from pixels.

| Surface | What OpenAdapt reads | Validated on |
|---|---|---|
| Web apps | The screen, plus the page's DOM | OpenEMR and openIMIS test copies, plus required CI on every build |
| Windows apps | The screen, plus UI Automation | 3 of 3 saves in a WinForms test app |
| macOS apps | The screen, plus Accessibility | 3 of 3 saves in TextEdit |
| Linux apps (X11) | The screen, plus AT-SPI | A GTK3 app in CI |
| Remote desktop (RDP) | The screen | 3 of 3 trials into Windows 11 over a real network |
| Citrix | The screen | A Citrix stand-in app with no DOM: 3 healthy runs, 3 stops on drift |

Each application on each surface needs its own qualification.
[Surfaces](https://docs.openadapt.ai/explanation/surfaces/) and [Limits](https://docs.openadapt.ai/explanation/limits/)
have the details.

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S["Record, or let an agent do it once"] --> C["Compile"] --> Q["Certify and qualify"] --> A["Admit"] --> R["Run with checks"]
    R -.->|"stopped: approve a fix"| C
```

For each step the compiler uses the most reliable layer the app offers: page
structure first (DOM, Windows UI Automation, macOS Accessibility, Linux
AT-SPI), a direct API call where one is bound, and pixels (template, text and
layout matching) only where nothing else exists, such as a remote desktop.
Qualification runs the program against normal and fault cases before an
admission lets that exact version run. At each save the program checks that
the right record is on screen, makes the entry, and reads the record back.

## How it compares

| | Computer-use agent | Agent with a replay cache | Traditional RPA | OpenAdapt |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| How you define the task | A goal in plain language | One agent run | A script or flow built in a designer | A person's recording or an agent's run |
| What runs each time | A model chooses each step from the screen | The recorded steps; the agent takes over on a miss | The fixed script | A compiled program you can read |
| Model calls per run | At least one per step | None on a hit; the agent's calls on a miss | None | None with default settings |
| When the screen changes | The model tries to adapt | The agent improvises live | A selector stops matching, or matches the wrong control | The run stops before saving; a fix is proposed and a person approves it |
| Right record? | The model judges from the screen | Usually only that the screen looks as recorded | Whatever the developer scripted | Checked before every save |
| Did the save land? | The model judges from the screen | The screen | Whatever the developer scripted | Read back from the system of record |
| Strongest for | New or changing tasks | Repeated tasks where a wrong save is cheap | Stable processes with a team to maintain the scripts | The same entry many times, where a wrong save is costly |

## What it can do

- **Learns from any successful run**, a person's demonstration or a computer-use agent's verified run, and compiles it into a program that runs with no model calls.
- **Uses the most reliable layer the app allows**: page structure (DOM, UI Automation, Accessibility), direct API calls where one is bound, and pixels only for remote desktops.
- **Builds branching programs** from several demonstrations, repeated halts and background runs, and routes each item to the right verified variant.
- **Works across surfaces**: web, Windows, macOS, Linux and RDP backends, chained in one workflow.
- **Confirms the right record before every write and reads the saved record back** from the system of record, never just the screen.
- **Stops instead of guessing**, never retries an uncertain save, and says what changed before a stop.
- **Binds each approval to exactly what will be saved**, with one-tap answers on a paired phone.
- **Repairs itself when the app changes**, probing a fix up to the save and asking a person to approve it.
- **Works as a safety layer under any agent**: MCP tools, a guarded save, Agent Skills and a CLI.
- **Runs locally**: no model calls on healthy runs, patient data redacted, signed receipts.

[CAPABILITIES.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/CAPABILITIES.md) has the evidence and code for each.

## What your agent gets back

| You see | `transaction_outcome` | An agent gets | What happens next |
|---|---|---|---|
| Done and checked | `VERIFIED` | `done` | Nothing. Only this result gets a shareable receipt. |
| Stopped before saving | `HALTED_BEFORE_EFFECT` | `needs_review` | Fix the cause, or show the program the fix, and run again. |
| Check the record | `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` | `not_sure_if_saved` | A save may have gone through. A person checks the record before anything is retried. |
| Finished, not checked | `COMPLETED_UNVERIFIED` | `not_sure_if_saved` | Fine for testing; not a production success. |
| Saved, waiting for its check | `SAVED_AWAITING_CHECK` | `not_sure_if_saved` | The save's check is a later report (a claim acknowledgment, an export). Don't rerun it. `openadapt-flow deferred settle` counts it as done only when the report confirms it. |
| Didn't run | `REJECTED_POLICY`, `CANCELED`, `FAILED_PLATFORM` | `did_not_run` | Fix the gate or the environment and run again. |

The console's last line can read `HALTED` for both the second and third rows.
`transaction_outcome` in `report.json` tells them apart, so base every rerun on
it. [Run outcomes](https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/outcomes/) lists every value.

## When to use something else

- **The app has an API for the task.** Call the API.
- **Every task is new.** Use a computer-use agent. OpenAdapt pays off when the
  same entry repeats.
- **There's no way to read the record back.** The record check needs read
  access to the system of record: an API, the database, FHIR, or a separate
  signed-in session. Without one, a run can only end as finished but not
  checked.


## Packages

`pip install openadapt` installs the `openadapt` command, the engine, and the
MCP server. The product packages live in this repository:

| Package (PyPI) | What it is | Source |
|---|---|---|
| [`openadapt`](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt/) | The `openadapt` command | [`openadapt/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/openadapt) |
| [`openadapt-flow`](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt-flow/) | The engine: record, compile, check, qualify, run, repair | [`packages/flow/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/packages/flow) |
| [`openadapt-agent`](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt-agent/) | The MCP server and Agent Skills | [`packages/agent/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/packages/agent) |
| [`openadapt-types`](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt-types/) | Shared request, result, and receipt models | [`packages/types/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/packages/types) |
| [`openadapt-capture`](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt-capture/) | The desktop recorder: `openadapt[capture]` | [`packages/capture/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/packages/capture) |
| [`openadapt-privacy`](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt-privacy/) | Finds and redacts personal and health data: `openadapt[privacy]` | [`packages/privacy/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/packages/privacy) |
| [`openadapt-desktop`](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt-desktop/) | OpenAdapt Desktop ([download](https://openadapt.ai/download)) | [`packages/desktop/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/packages/desktop) |
| [`openadapt-tray`](https://pypi.org/project/openadapt-tray/) | Menu-bar and system-tray controls and status for OpenAdapt Desktop | [`packages/tray/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/packages/tray) |

Each package installs only what it imports. For example, `pip install openadapt-privacy` doesn't install the engine or the desktop app. CI checks each package's install size and dependency list ([install weight](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/docs/monorepo/INSTALL_WEIGHT.md)).

Research on GUI agents lives in separate repositories:
[openadapt-evals](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/openadapt-evals) (benchmarks)
and [openadapt-ml](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/openadapt-ml) (model
training). The [packages map](https://docs.openadapt.ai/reference/packages/) has the full list.

## Security and procurement

Screens, typed values, and recordings stay on the computer or runner that runs
OpenAdapt. The shareable receipt and the Cloud dashboard hold counts, digests,
and closed values. A sanitized copy leaves only after a person approves it, and
screenshots go to a model host only if you turn on model grounding.
[Security & procurement](https://docs.openadapt.ai/security/) covers data handling, deployment
boundaries, evidence, subprocessors, and release integrity. Plans are on the
[pricing page](https://openadapt.ai/pricing).

The signed ledger has seven active target admissions. Their evidence class
is `remote-safe-synthetic`, not MockMed `production_acceptance`. They remain
valid until revoked; there's no expiry date. `pip install openadapt` is the
admitted runtime (launcher 1.16.0, Flow 1.35.1). Desktop's admitted artifact
is the 0.16.0 wheel. Native Mac DMGs stay ad-hoc signed 0.15.0; don't treat
those as admitted. A Production run still needs a workflow admission for the
exact compiled bundle, application, and environment.
[Check the live signed Production record](https://docs.openadapt.ai/production-lifecycle.json).

# What OpenAdapt can do

OpenAdapt turns work that people or computer-use agents do in applications
with no usable API (EMRs, payer portals, desktop and remote-desktop apps) into
programs that make the same entry every time with no model calls, check that
the entry landed in the right record, and stop instead of guessing.

This page indexes what OpenAdapt implements, with the status, the evidence and
the code for each capability:

- [Ten capabilities](#openadapt-in-ten-capabilities) and [often missed](#often-missed)
- [The core: a checked entry](#the-core-a-checked-entry-every-time),
  [approvals](#approvals), [branching work](#branching-work-not-one-linear-path)
- [Surfaces](#surfaces), [the fastest layer](#the-fastest-layer-the-app-allows),
  [when the app changes](#when-the-app-changes)
- [Computer-use agents](#computer-use-agents),
  [recording, privacy and proof](#recording-privacy-and-proof)
- [Every command](#every-command-by-capability) and
  [measured results](#measured-results)

## OpenAdapt in ten capabilities

Each capability is implemented in the
[OpenAdapt monorepo](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt). "Released"
means it ships in the current PyPI packages; "on main" means merged into the
monorepo and installable from source.

1. **Learns from any successful run, a person's or an agent's.** A person
   records a task, or a computer-use agent does it once and OpenAdapt compiles
   the verified run into a program (`openadapt_flow.jit`, released;
   prompt-to-program `compile-agent`, on main; the agent can act through code
   instead of screenshots, [#1305](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1305)). Agents can drive the recording
   through the web, native Windows, RDP and Citrix backends. An agent connected over MCP can
   teach itself a new workflow and then call it as a tool
   (`openadapt-agent serve --teach`,
   [#1335](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1335)).
2. **Compiles to the fastest layer the app allows.** Page structure first (DOM,
   Windows UI Automation, macOS Accessibility), direct API calls where the app's
   own traffic allows them (`ApiActuator`, released; compiled from captured
   traffic in [#1261](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1261)),
   and pixels only
   where nothing else exists, such as a remote desktop. It is not a pixel-macro
   recorder.
3. **Builds branching programs, not one linear path.** One program from several
   demonstrations (`induce`, `disambiguate`), a branch learned from several
   halts fixed the same way (`teach-branch`), candidate branches mined from many
   real runs in the background (shadow mode,
   [#1212](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1212)), and a router
   that sends each item to the right verified variant. Shadow mining and the
   router are on main; the rest is released.
4. **Works across surfaces in one workflow.** Backends for web, native Windows
   and macOS, Linux, RDP and Citrix. Programs chain across surfaces passing confirmed values
   (`compose`, `process`, released), and one program can switch surfaces, tabs
   and popups mid-run ([#1197](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1197)).
5. **Confirms the right record before every write and reads it back after.**
   The record check reads the system of record (API, database, FHIR with SMART
   Backend Services, or a separate signed-in session), never just the screen.
   `record --verify` proposes those checks from what the demonstration changed.
   Released.
6. **Stops instead of improvising, and never retries an uncertain save.** A run
   that can't prove a save ends `HALTED_BEFORE_EFFECT` or
   `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED`, never "success". A ledger of what changed before
   a stop, with undo steps a person approves, is on main. The rest is
   released.
7. **Approvals are bound to exactly what will be saved.** Each save waits for a
   person by default and can be answered on a paired phone with one card per
   decision. The approval is bound to the exact screenshot and form state, and
   the form is read again before saving, so what was approved is what is saved.
   Person-signed grants let named agents answer. Released.
8. **Repairs itself, with a person approving.** Governed repair (propose,
   review, campaign, canary, rollback), agent-demonstrated fixes for a halted
   run, and fleet drift patches shared with no patient data are released.
   Self-repair, where an agent proposes a fix and Flow probes it up to the save
   without saving, is on main, and so are fixes of up to three new steps.
9. **Is a safety layer underneath any agent.** An agent's MCP calls, a task
   ledger that keeps a long job's rules, items, questions and checked saves on
   the server ([#1332](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1332)), a guarded save around any agent's write
   ([#1258](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1258)), a guard for
   an agent you already run that holds its browser's saves with no change to
   the agent ([#1357](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1357)), `verify-run`
   to judge any executor's write from the system of record, and Agent Skills and
   a CLI for coding agents. Released except where a PR is named.
10. **Runs locally and keeps data private.** Healthy runs make no model calls
    and send nothing out. Personal and health data are redacted from text,
    screenshots and structure (scrub-by-default for anything that leaves the
    machine is on main); a strict no-outbound mode, an unattended on-prem
    service, and signed, timestamped receipts are released.

## Often missed

| What OpenAdapt does | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Learns branching programs from several demonstrations, from repeated halts, and from many background runs. | `induce`, `teach-branch`, [SHADOW_MINING.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/capture/docs/SHADOW_MINING.md), [LEARN_FROM_MANY_RUNS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/LEARN_FROM_MANY_RUNS.md) |
| Chains programs across surfaces, and one program can switch surfaces, tabs and popups mid-run. | `compose`, `process`, [#1197](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1197) |
| Uses page structure first on web, Windows, macOS and Linux, with pixels as the fallback for remote desktops. Benchmarks labelled "vision-only" ran a deliberately pixel-only arm. | [RESOLUTION_LADDER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/RESOLUTION_LADDER.md) |
| Replaces a single HTML form submission with the request the app itself sends, compiled from the network traffic captured while recording, then reads the record back. JSON or GraphQL requests, multi-step wizards and governed runs still use the screen steps. | `api`, [API_TIER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/API_TIER.md) |
| Builds the record check itself. After a save, the app usually reads the record back to show it; `scaffold-verifier` finds that read in the captured traffic or a read-only database, builds the check from it and tries to break it before a person reviews it. No API or SQL needs to be written by hand. | [EFFECT_KIT.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/EFFECT_KIT.md#a-record-check-built-from-the-apps-own-reads-scaffold-verifier) |
| Checks a save on desktop, RDP and Citrix apps with no API at all, by looking the record up in the app's own screens in a separate session. | [EFFECT_KIT.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/EFFECT_KIT.md#separate-session-desktop-read-back-desktop_readback) |
| Keeps pixel-path runs working across display scaling from 100% to 175% and font smoothing on or off, and stops rather than saves when the record changed. | [benchmark/pixel_scale](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/pixel_scale/README.md) |
| Lists every change made before a stop and rolls it back with compensations a person approved once, then proves it by reading the whole database: equal to the read from before the run is `ROLLED_BACK`, anything else names the exact rows. | `undo`, `rollback`, [ROLLBACK.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/ROLLBACK.md), [AFTER_A_STOP.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/AFTER_A_STOP.md) |
| Repairs itself when the app changes: governed repair, agent-demonstrated fixes, fleet patches, and self-repair probed up to the save. | [REPAIR_LIFECYCLE.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/REPAIR_LIFECYCLE.md) |
| Repairs a change that needs new steps, such as a new required dialog or a control moved into a menu: up to three new steps, each with its own record check, probed up to the save before one person approves. | [SELF_REPAIR.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/SELF_REPAIR.md), [#1325](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1325) |
| Compiles a computer-use agent's verified run, with no human demonstration needed. | [JIT.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/JIT.md) |
| The agent that does a task once can act through code, not a screenshot-and-click loop: it reads the page or accessibility tree, acts by role and name, keeps notes with a sandboxed read-only shell, and asks for a screenshot only when it needs one. It is arm 7 of the scoreboard. | `CODE_AS_ACTION.md` in [#1305](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1305) |
| Binds each approval to the exact screenshot and form state, and re-reads the form before saving. | [APPROVAL_MODES.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/APPROVAL_MODES.md) |
| Has a written threat model for prompt injection against the agent that teaches or repairs a program, with tests. | [THREAT_MODEL.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/THREAT_MODEL.md) |
| Fills inputs from a referral PDF, fax image or email, and holds back anything unclear for a person. | `intake`, [INTAKE.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/INTAKE.md) |
| Ships as one monorepo with separately installable packages (flow, agent, types, capture, privacy, desktop and tray), each released from the monorepo. | [README](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/README.md) |
| Makes no model calls on healthy runs. Model training (openadapt-ml) is separate research. | [README](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/README.md) |

## The full map

Every capability, with its status, its evidence and where it lives.

Status:

- **Released**: in the current PyPI release (openadapt-flow 2.2.0).
- **On main**: merged into the monorepo; installable from source.

Evidence:

- **Real app**: run against a real third-party application, such as a local
  OpenEMR or openIMIS.
- **Synthetic**: run against OpenAdapt's own test apps (MockMed and fixtures).

All patient and claim data in every test and benchmark is synthetic.

## The core: a checked entry, every time

A person, or a computer-use agent once, shows a task. OpenAdapt compiles it
into a program that makes the same entry every time with no model calls. It
confirms the right record before acting, reads the saved record back from the
system of record instead of trusting the screen, and stops instead of
improvising or retrying when something is off.

| Capability | Status | Evidence | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compile one or more demonstrations into a deterministic program | Released | Real app (OpenEMR referral, 62 timed runs) | `openadapt-flow record`, `compile`; [packages/flow](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/README.md) |
| Classify common local edits without a person (select-all, Enter in a field or dropdown, an in-form tab, an informational dialog's dismiss), only when the recording's network capture shows no write and a runtime check confirms only the expected change | On main ([#1366](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1366)) | Synthetic; OpenEMR referral recording re-admitted offline (violations 12 to 1 under `permissive`) | [LOCAL_EDIT_CLASSIFICATION.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/design/LOCAL_EDIT_CLASSIFICATION.md), `compiler/local_edit.py` |
| Right-record check before any write (structure, then OCR, then pixels) | Released | Real app and synthetic | [RESOLUTION_LADDER.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/RESOLUTION_LADDER.md), `runtime/identity.py` |
| Read the saved record back from the system of record (API, database, FHIR, separate session) | Released | Real app (OpenEMR 12 of 12 fields) | [VERIFICATION.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/VERIFICATION.md), `runtime/effects/` |
| Read values out of an app as a workflow step (READ), with a records format, a signed review queue and export to CSV or a database | On main ([#1229](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1229), [#1215](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1215), [#1218](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1218)–[#1224](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1224)) | Synthetic (mock desktop apps) | `openadapt_flow/interchange/` |
| Stop before the effect instead of improvising (`HALTED_BEFORE_EFFECT`) | Released | Real app and synthetic | `runtime/replayer.py` |
| Never retry an uncertain save (`RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED`) | Released | Synthetic (fault server) | [VERIFICATION.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/VERIFICATION.md) |
| One check-level scale, 0 to 5, from "unchecked" to "counterparty confirmed" | Released | Unit tests | `openadapt_flow/check_level.py` |
| Judge any executor's write, including an agent's or a script's, from the system of record | Released | Synthetic | `openadapt-flow verify-run`, [VERIFY_RUN.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/VERIFY_RUN.md) |
| Judge an "ensure the record exists" write (found, created once with every value, or needs review) through a FHIR server's read path only: searches, AuditEvent and `_history`, never the database; the coverage claim names that read path. An agent's own correction of the record it created counts as one write when the audit trail and history show only that agent, no other reader, and the same record in every version | On main ([#1640](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1640), corrections [#1655](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1655)) | Real app (Medplum 5.2.8; three blind fault suites: 17/18, 17/20, 19/20; no fault passed in the last two. Corrections, on 15 blind cases and the 37 public ones: false stops 8 to 2 and 9 to 4 for Claude, no harm passed that the old rule caught) | `openadapt_flow/ensure_record.py`, [ENSURE_RECORD.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/ENSURE_RECORD.md) |
| Generate an ensure-record contract from three demonstrations, the server's CapabilityStatement and its SearchParameter definitions: field paths and `[system=…]` filters, comparison kinds, value maps, identity, search parameters, the closed record and the change feed. It refuses when unsure, asks a person to confirm an identity for a type with no reviewed template, and self-checks every demonstration plus a perturbation per field | On main ([#1653](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1653)) | Real app (Medplum 5.2.8: all 16 hand-written Patient lines regenerated; one blind write type, Immunization: 78 s of person time, 2 lines edited after the person declined the proposed identity; blind suite 23/24, no fault passed) | `openadapt_flow/generate/ensure_contract.py`, [RESULTS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/contract_autogen/results/RESULTS.md) |
| A stop card for a stopped write: the exact record difference and who else wrote, with Undo or Fix that reads back, or Open in the app; cost modelled from published operators and timed machine steps, as pre-registered | On main ([#1653](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1653)) | Real app (Medplum 5.2.8, blind suite: 16 stops, 14 one-tap with no failed read-back; modelled 42 s per caught harm against 420; one wrong category on a false stop, gone in the re-measure with `void`: 24/24, 15 stops, no wrong category, no failed read-back) | `benchmark/stop_card/`, [PREREG_REVIEW.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/stop_card/PREREG_REVIEW.md) |
| Generate `openadapt.verify/v1` contracts from a MySQL, MariaDB or PostgreSQL schema, the kinds of write with their parameter names, and one demonstration write per example: one contract per field set (an update gets one for each set of fields it may change), list parameters by length, a `found` twin for a record already in place, the whole-database frame on MySQL and MariaDB, rows the app adds on its own declared by count, a recheck window the person confirms, and `frame.versions` (a lost update) from a version column or the app's audit trail of saves. Every undecided point is one numbered question; every contract is loaded and dry-read against the live store before it is written; a needed `TRIGGER` grant or view is applied with a flag or the kind is refused. Not yet: OpenAPI metadata | On main ([#1672](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1672)) | Real app (first study, instance copies; questions for a person: Dolibarr 3, Redmine 1, EspoCRM 2, against 11 hand decisions each; every in-scope planted fault stopped; see [RESULTS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/generate_contracts/RESULTS.md)) | `python -m openadapt_flow.generate.verify_contract`, [GENERATE_CONTRACTS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/GENERATE_CONTRACTS.md) |
| `void` in an ensure-record contract: values that make a record assert nothing (`status="entered-in-error"`). A record holding one is never the person, is not a duplicate, and a created one needs review; it names values to leave out, never values to keep, and can't name an identity field | On main ([#1657](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1657)) | Real app (Medplum 5.2.8: 8 live cases written in advance, 8/8 with the line, 5/8 and one silent pass without it; frozen blind Immunization suite 24/24); adversarial review recorded | `openadapt_flow/ensure_record.py`, [RESULTS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/fhir_medplum/void/results/RESULTS.md), [REVIEW_VOID.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/fhir_medplum/void/REVIEW_VOID.md) |
| Check a patient registration on a commercial EHR through its public FHIR sandbox: Epic (open.epic, R4), read through FHIR search and read with SMART backend auth; the frame is the search set, since the sandbox has no AuditEvent or `_history` | On main ([#1656](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1656)) | Real app (Epic public sandbox, August 2026 release; blind round 12/13 with none passed as verified, the miss a false refusal fixed in the contract; caught Epic dropping the phone on a 201 create) | `benchmark/commercial_ehr/`, [FINDINGS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/commercial_ehr/FINDINGS.md) |
| A public benchmark a vendor reruns with their own agent: `openadapt bench medplum --agent <scripted|claude|cmd:...|py:...>` runs 37 written-for-it cases (Patient, AllergyIntolerance, Appointment) against a local Medplum through a fault proxy, and scores the agent's claim, a read-back and OpenAdapt's verifier against an end-state oracle | On main ([#1652](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1652)) | Real app (Medplum 5.2.8; Claude Sonnet 5.5: OpenAdapt missed 1 of 9 harms with 4 false stops, all corrections that changed the record's identity, against 8 missed by the claim and the read-back; cold run from clone to scorecard 5 min) | [README](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/fhir_medplum/public/README.md), [RESULTS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/fhir_medplum/public/RESULTS.md) |
| Prove that nothing outside the declared change moved (frame conditions), and attribute concurrent edits by other users through the app's audit log (by record, or by owner for a user's own rows such as their UI settings) or a modified-by field; the receipt signs which parts were checked | On main | Synthetic (MockMed, SQLite audit log) | `verify-run`, [VERIFICATION_COVERAGE.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/VERIFICATION_COVERAGE.md) |
| Admit a record check only after a fault suite written to a store copy shows it catches every fault class it claims, including writes outside its read (another table, a side row for the saved record), and sign each class's result into the receipt | On main | Synthetic (in-memory REST store, SQLite copy); OpenEMR stand-in built from the pinned fixture's dump | `openadapt_flow/fault_gate.py`, `scaffold-verifier --fault-gate`, `verify-run` `admission:` |
| Check that the saved record matches its source document, not only the parameters: intake keeps each value's line, a second reading must agree before a guarded save, and a round trip compares the read-back with the document | On main | Synthetic (MockMed, text referral) | `openadapt_flow/provenance.py`, `intake`, `verify-run --provenance`, guarded save |
| Check one write from Python, without the CLI: one API (`openadapt_flow.verifier`: `begin_write`, `verify_write`; 2.4.1's `capture` form still works, deprecated) with one outcome (`CONFIRMED`, `REFUTED`, `UNCERTAIN`), the receipt, which parts were checked, and the result's scope (read path, stores read, time window, what it doesn't cover) | On main | Synthetic (SQLite; MockMed's fault server over real HTTP) | `openadapt_flow/verifier.py`, [VERIFIER_API.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/VERIFIER_API.md) |
| Never send a write twice while its outcome is unknown: an append-only ledger on local disk (pluggable backend), keyed by the write's identity, that every adapter, the MCP tools and the CLI consult before sending; a read-back against the attempt's own baseline resolves it, and a refuted write waits for a person (`openadapt verify ledger list`, `reconcile`, `release`) | On main | Synthetic (MockMed's fault server: a worker killed between the send and the read-back, killed during a timed-out send, killed before the send, a late write, and two worker processes started together on one write) | `openadapt_flow/write_ledger.py`, [VERIFIER_API.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/VERIFIER_API.md#the-uncertain-write-ledger) |
| Catch a write that lands after the verdict (a background job, a trigger, a delayed side record): a `CONFIRMED` with a recheck due is provisional (`provisional`, `recheck_due_at`); the recheck reads the whole database again and refutes the earlier result when a change since the post-save read has no explanation, and a recheck that doesn't confirm holds the write in the ledger. Run it from Python (`verifier.recheck`) or MCP (`verify_recheck`). A write after the recheck's read is not seen (`frame.database.recheck_after_s`, no default window) | On main ([#1639](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1639)); provisional result, MCP tool and ledger hold ([#1669](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1669)) | Real app (Dolibarr 21 and EspoCRM 10 on MariaDB 11.4, 180 s window: 4 of 4 planted late writes at 125 to 130 s refuted at the recheck, correct writes confirmed; EspoCRM's cron daemon needs its job tables declared; Redmine 6.1 on PostgreSQL 17, 180 s window: the first-contact study's late writes F19 and F20 refuted at the recheck, correct writes confirmed); synthetic (SQLite); opt-in live OpenEMR test | `openadapt_flow/verifier.py`, `runtime/effects/late_write.py`, [VERIFY_RUN.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/VERIFY_RUN.md#writes-that-land-later) |
| Diff the whole database for the frame (`frame.database`) on SQLite, MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL. On MySQL and MariaDB every column type is read exactly (binary strings, `BIT`, geometries and vectors as hex, `FLOAT` widened to `DOUBLE`, `JSON` as stored text, decimals at full precision). On PostgreSQL every column type is read as text by a declared rule in a session pinned to UTC and exact float output, and a type without a rule, a table the account can't read in full, or an unreadable sequence is refused. So a row the save adds, changes or removes outside the declared records, such as an extra planned call or a stream note, is refuted unless a declared effect, a side record, an attributed concurrent write or an allow-listed bookkeeping table explains it | On main ([#1661](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1661)); PostgreSQL ([#1673](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1673)) | Real app (Dolibarr 21 on MariaDB 11.4: all 387 tables read where the frame raised `TypeError`; EspoCRM on MariaDB 11.4: the first-contact study's extra call and stream note refuted, correct opportunities verified; Redmine 6.1 on PostgreSQL 17: 58 tables read, a stray upload in a table the contract doesn't read refuted, correct writes verified); live MariaDB and PostgreSQL type tests | [VERIFY_RUN.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/VERIFY_RUN.md#the-whole-database), `runtime/effects/db_snapshot.py` |
| Catch a lost update: another user saves a change to the record while the agent works, and the agent saves its stale copy over it. Before and after look like a correct update, so `frame.versions` reads the target's versions (FHIR or SQL version history, a version column, or the app's audit or action-history table) before and after the write. A version by another author, or more than one version step when no author is read, refutes the write; a version that can't be read or attributed stops it | On main ([#1662](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1662)) | Real app (HAPI FHIR and EspoCRM, first-contact study fault scripts: both lost updates refuted, correct updates verified, every other case's verdict unchanged) | [VERIFY_RUN.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/VERIFY_RUN.md#lost-updates), `runtime/effects/versions.py` |
| Guarded save: a safety layer any agent wraps around one write (check the record, hold for approval, read back) | On main ([#1258](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1258)) | Synthetic | `GUARDED_SAVE.md` |
| A person's approval in Desktop is signed with a key kept behind Touch ID on a Mac: one-prompt setup in the app, a prompt for every answer, and Flow never sees the key | On main ([#1500](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1500)) | Unit tests; opt-in test on a real Secure Enclave | `packages/desktop/openadapt_desktop/approver_keychain.py`, [APPROVAL_MODES.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/APPROVAL_MODES.md#the-approver-key) |
| The approver root Desktop trusts can be pinned by an administrator, in a file this user can't write (macOS, Linux, Windows); Desktop checks the owner, mode or ACL and refuses links. A Mac without one uses the root it set up behind Touch ID, read with Keychain prompts off; the two disagreeing is refused | On main | Unit tests per attack on real files; Windows ACL rules unit-tested, real-ACL test on Windows CI; opt-in test against the real login Keychain | `openadapt-desktop approver-pin`, `packages/desktop/openadapt_desktop/approver_anchor.py`, [APPROVAL_MODES.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/APPROVAL_MODES.md#the-approver-key) |
| Review stops: every stop as one card with the evidence side by side (the item next to each possible match, field by field), answered with one key or tap on the computer or a paired phone, signed with the approver key, with batches for similar stops. The queue presents and collects; a changed or expired card changes nothing | On main ([#1519](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1519)) | Unit tests; a keystroke-level estimate on 20 soak stops (26.7 s to 8.2 s to decide, a model, not a person) | `packages/desktop/openadapt_desktop/stop_queue.py`, [benchmark/stop_queue](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/desktop/benchmark/stop_queue/README.md) |
| Draft a record check from the demonstration's write steps (`scaffold-verifier`) | Released | Synthetic | `openadapt-flow scaffold-verifier` (a person fills in the draft) |
| Build a working record check from the reads the app made while the person viewed the saved record, and test it against injected bad writes before anyone reviews it | On main ([#1284](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1284)) | Synthetic (MockMed, OpenEMR fixture) | `openadapt-flow scaffold-verifier` |
| Check a save on desktop, RDP or Citrix by looking the record up in a separate read-only session | On main ([#1280](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1280)) | Synthetic (WinForms, RDP and Citrix stand-ins) | `runtime/effects/` |
| Learn the record check from the recording, when the person looks the record up after saving | On main ([#1290](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1290)) | Synthetic | `record --verify` |
| A record check's duplicate key can be several fields together, such as last name, first name and birth date: the check fails when more than one record carries all of them, counting records that were already there | On main ([#1393](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/issues/1393)) | Synthetic (OpenEMR-shaped patient rows) | verify.yaml `record.duplicate_key: [lname, fname, DOB]`, `confirm_params(idempotency_key=[...])`, `Effect.composite_key` |
| Checked later: a save confirmed by a later report or acknowledgment, never counted as done until then | On main ([#1297](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1297)) | Synthetic | `SAVED_AWAITING_CHECK` |
| Keep the server's own answer to a save as lower-level evidence on the receipt | On main ([#1298](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1298)) | Synthetic | receipts |
| A ledger of what changed before a stop, a write-ordering lint, and undo steps a person approves | On main ([#1263](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1263)) | Synthetic (MockMed) | change ledger |
| Propose an undo for each saving step (another recording, captured traffic, or the old value), keep it only if a test copy shows every record restored, and offer it after a stop once a person approves it | On main ([#1346](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1346)) | Synthetic (MockMed, MockLoan, live browser) | `openadapt-flow undo propose`, `undo accept`; [AFTER_A_STOP.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/AFTER_A_STOP.md) |
| Roll a stopped run back on its own: the approved compensation for each change, latest first, an uncertain write only when a fresh read shows it landed, then a read of the whole database: every row the run touched back as it was and nothing else changed (`ROLLED_BACK`), or the exact rows a person repairs (`RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED`). A compensation runs only while every change in the store is positively the run's own by the app's audit log, so another user's work is never compensated away, and a hard delete runs only where the deployment allows it (void, restore or discard otherwise). `rollback qualify` stops the run before and after every save on a test copy and keeps only compensations that restore the whole store | On main ([#1634](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1634)) | MockMed, live browser through the CLI; SQLite whole-database tests | `openadapt-flow rollback qualify`, `rollback:` in deployment.yaml; [ROLLBACK.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/ROLLBACK.md) |
| Leave the screen clean after an item that halted before any write: close dialogs and cancel forms with the recordings' own controls, re-enter, confirm the start screen and read the records back before the session takes another item. A session that doesn't come back is marked dirty and takes no more items; a cleanup that changed a record makes the item's write uncertain and stops the run. `cleanup qualify` tries the cleanup after every step on a test copy and refuses one that changes a record | On main ([#1607](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1607)) | Synthetic (scripted three-screen app through the real replayer and pool) and real app (pinned OpenEMR: a halted New Patient item left the confirmation dialog open; re-entry closed it, the form was empty, no patient row changed and the next item's first steps ran with no model calls; a signed-out screen was marked dirty; [results](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/halt_cleanup/results/openemr.json)) | `openadapt-flow cleanup qualify`; [HALT_CLEANUP.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/HALT_CLEANUP.md) |

Web, and Windows, macOS, Linux, RDP and Citrix with a person approving each save | On main ([#1335](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1335)) | Synthetic (MockMed over MCP, and through the real RDP and Citrix backends) | `openadapt-agent serve --teach`, [packages/agent](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/agent/README.md#teach-a-new-workflow-from-your-agent) |
| Turn a read-only browser task into a tool for the coding agent you already use: `openadapt setup` registers the MCP server and a skill in Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Gemini CLI (idempotent, `--dry-run`, `--undo`); the agent does the task once through `teach_start`/`teach_act`/`teach_finish`, the task must end in a download, the file is checked (columns, a column between two inputs or equal to one, fewest rows), the compiled steps are replayed once with no model, and the agent gets a `taught_<name>` tool that downloads a checked file with new inputs. The browser sends no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE and stays on one site; a compiled run stops when a control is missing, matches more than one element, or is relabelled | On main ([#1502](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1502)) | Real headless Chromium on the local example portal (scripted MCP client, in CI); a real Claude Code agent taught the export from the guide's prompt and called the tool with new dates (2026-10-24, one run) | `openadapt setup`, `openadapt-agent serve --teach-browser`, [FIRST_TOOL.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/FIRST_TOOL.md) |
| Verify any agent's own writes: `openadapt verify` reads the system of record before and after a write, against a contract the operator owns (REST, FHIR, SQL, GraphQL), and returns a verified receipt (`openadapt.effect-receipt/v1`) or a refusal (`REFUTED`, `UNCERTAIN`), never an unverified success. Python SDK (`openadapt.verify`, which is `openadapt_flow.verifier`: `begin_write`, `verify_write`, `verified_write`) wraps a write in any agent framework; the MCP server (`openadapt verify serve`) offers `verify_begin`, `verify_check` and `verify_recheck` to any MCP client | On main ([#1589](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1589)) | Synthetic (MockMed's fault server over real HTTP: correct write, wrong record, not saved, saved twice, unreadable store) | `openadapt verify`, [VERIFY_WRITES.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/VERIFY_WRITES.md) |
| Skill cache for framework agents: an agent in any framework does a browser task through compile-agent's harness as plain tools (`BrowserTools`); when the system of record shows exactly the task's record and the operator confirms the checks, the run is canaried, admitted and emitted as an MCP server. A repeat of the same task (instruction, record, app, contract, environment) calls that tool instead of the agent: no model calls, the program's checks and this task's record check on every run, eviction after a failed run | On main | Synthetic (MockMed, LangGraph on `claude-sonnet-5-5`, 3 trials, repeats on the same record: run 1 6 model calls and $0.022; runs 2 to 10 27/27 VERIFIED, 0 model calls, 7.8 s median); Trac 1.6: run 1 verified, not admitted | `openadapt_flow.integrations.agents.skills`, [benchmark/skill_cache](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/skill_cache/README.md) |
| Verified write tools for agent frameworks: `verified(tool, contract=...)` wraps a Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph or CrewAI write tool in one line. The contract and any values the operator pins come from the operator, never the agent's arguments; the store is read before and after; the agent gets a receipt or a refusal, and a refused write is held instead of retried | On main | Synthetic (each framework's own agent loop with a scripted model, writing through the example app's order form over real HTTP: verified save, a save the app drops, a save it keeps twice); one real-model run per framework, opt-in | `openadapt_flow.integrations.agents`, extras `claude-agent-sdk`, `openai-agents`, `langgraph` (CrewAI: install `crewai` beside it); [AGENT_FRAMEWORKS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/AGENT_FRAMEWORKS.md) |
| Teach a browser write as a verified tool: with write contracts (`serve --teach-browser --contracts DIR`), the agent teaches a save once; run 1 is verified in the system of record before the `taught_<name>` tool exists, and every call makes the write and returns a verified receipt or a refusal. Sign-in values come from the server's environment and never reach the agent or the program. Controls in named iframes are found through their frame | On main ([#1589](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1589)) | Synthetic (the example app's sign-in and order form in headless Chromium over MCP: verified save, a save the app drops, a save it keeps twice) | `openadapt-agent serve --teach-browser --contracts`, [VERIFY_WRITES.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/VERIFY_WRITES.md#teach-a-write-as-a-tool) |
| Guard an agent you already run: attach to its own Chromium over CDP (one added line), hold each save until the record on screen is the one the task names, block it and tell the agent why when it isn't, read the save back; a run that reads back correctly becomes a draft program with a record check from scaffold-verifier, which a person confirms and admits, then a `taught_*` tool with no model calls. `--observe-only` never blocks | On main ([#1357](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1357), stacked on [#1335](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1335)) | Synthetic (MockMed, scripted Playwright agent, `effect_e2e` faults) | `openadapt-flow guard`, [GUARD_AN_AGENT.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/GUARD_AN_AGENT.md) |
| Task ledger per job: rules locked when the job opens and enforced on every run, item status set only from OpenAdapt's own results, and yes-or-no questions a person answers on the phone or in Desktop, including when a run stops | On main ([#1332](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1332)) | Synthetic (30-item MockMed worklist, scripted agent, no model calls) | MCP tools `open_job`, `get_job`, `add_items`, `record_evidence`, `ask_user`, `get_answer`, `change_constraint`, `close_job`; [Track a long job](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/agent/README.md#track-a-long-job) |
| Limit a teaching agent to the declared task on every teach path (`compile_agent`, `compile-agent`, teach over MCP, the airbag guard): typed text must be a declared value, links and browser requests to other origins are refused, writes are checked before they are sent, and the record is read back before a draft exists. Injected instructions in record notes, banners, tooltips, alt text and server responses are blocked or caught on MockMed through each path (scripted agent; a live-model mode is off by default). Self-repair refuses a control that leaves the app | On main ([#1359](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1359), [#1386](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1386)) | Synthetic | `openadapt_flow.teach_scope`, [THREAT_MODEL.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/THREAT_MODEL.md) |
| Compile an agent's first verified run from a prompt (`compile-agent`), and a code-as-action authoring agent | On main ([#1277](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1277), [#1305](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1305)); the agent harness behind it runs on every backend, on main ([#1283](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1283)) | Synthetic | `compile-agent` |
| Score harness optimizers (Harness², Meta-Harness) on GUI tasks with the record read-back as the reward, with full trace export | On main ([#1299](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1299), [#1300](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1300), [#1301](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1301)) | Synthetic (scripted proposer) | `integrations/harness2/` |
| One scoreboard comparing the agent alone with OpenAdapt across tasks (correctness by read-back, cost, time, items per hour) | On main ([#1303](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/pull/1303)) | Synthetic and local OpenEMR and openIMIS test copies | `benchmark/scoreboard/` |
| Pull a skill from the registry (`pull app/task@version`) and run it only after qualifying it on your own instance: `pull` marks it and expires any certification it carries, `skill bind` records your addresses and the names of the variables that hold credentials (never their values), `skill qualify` runs its bundled record check there, and `run`, `replay`, `emit-skill` and `emit-mcp` refuse it until then, and on any other instance. The index and its archives carry a keyless Sigstore attestation from the registry release workflow, checked offline against a pinned identity, and expire and can't be rolled back; a shipped record check runs no code and reads only your binding | On main | Unit tests | `openadapt-flow skill`, [SKILLS_REGISTRY.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/design/SKILLS_REGISTRY.md) |

## Every command, by capability

Each `openadapt-flow` command, grouped by the capability it serves. Each
command has one file under
[`packages/flow/docs/commands/`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/commands/): to add a
command, add `<group>/<verb>.md` and run `python scripts/build_command_map.py`.
A test fails when a command has no file or this list is out of date.

**Record and build a program:**

- `cleanup`: A clean screen after a halted item; `cleanup qualify` tries the halt cleanup on a test copy after every step and stores it when the start screen always comes back and no record changes.
- `fleet`
- `repair`

## Measured results

- **OpenEMR referral, 62 timed runs each, warm.** OpenAdapt took a median of
  29.7 s and a computer-use agent (Claude) 36.5 s. Both saved 62 of 63
  referrals correctly. OpenAdapt made no model calls; the agent cost about
  $0.08 per referral. Raw data and
  figures: [benchmark/openemr_referral_timing](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/openemr_referral_timing/).
- **Guard an agent you already run, MockMed.** A scripted Playwright agent
  in its own browser, 90 runs at a high shared load (median load average 29).
  Of the 8 `effect_e2e` faults that leave a wrong record, the agent alone
  reported 6 as saved; with the guard, the read-back caught 7 and 1 (a stray
  write to a table the REST read doesn't cover) got through; the compiled
  program caught all 8. The guard blocked the saves it can see: a save on the
  wrong patient and a second submit. Same-load pairs: the guarded agent took
  6.3 s (6 actions, each a model call for a real agent), the compiled tool
  4.4 s with no model calls:
  [GUARD_AN_AGENT.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/GUARD_AN_AGENT.md#measured-on-mockmed).
- **Fault test.** We injected 8 kinds of bad save, 9 runs each, alongside
  clean runs: 72 runs left a wrong record behind. A check that trusts the screen's "Saved" banner reported 54 of those
  as success; reading the record back over the app's REST API missed 9; the
  complete database read path caught all 72. The fault set and method are in
  [EFFECT_E2E.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/effect_e2e/EFFECT_E2E.md).
- **OpenEMR referral: agent, screen program and API step.** Median wall time
  per referral, from a fresh browser through sign-in, the entry and the read-back:
  agent alone 36.5 s (62 of 63 correct, the 14 to 15 Oct study); compiled program
  on the screen 22.5 s (18 of 18); the same program with the API step 3.3 s
  (18 of 18). The program rows ran on 19 Oct, interleaved on one copy, with
  the approval gate off; the benchmark harness admitted the API step:
  [SCOREBOARD.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/scoreboard/SCOREBOARD.md#openemr-agent-screen-program-and-api-step).
- **An agent's claims versus the read-back, on OpenEMR.** With faults injected
  in the fixture's database (partial, wrong value, duplicate, not persisted,
  another chart deleted, another chart edited; 5 items each), Claude Sonnet 5.5
  computer use claimed success on all 30 bad saves. `verify-run` caught 25 and
  confirmed 5 of 5 clean saves with no false alarms:
  [SCOREBOARD.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/scoreboard/SCOREBOARD.md#the-agents-claims-versus-the-read-back).
- **An agent's claims versus the read-back.** Claude Sonnet 5.5 computer use,
  working alone on a test app whose server broke the save in 6 ways (5 items
  each), reported all 30 bad saves as done. `verify-run` flagged all 30 and
  confirmed all 10 clean saves, with no false alarms. The app shows "saved"
  before the server answers, so this measures what the screen can't show, not
  the agent's care:
  [SCOREBOARD.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/scoreboard/SCOREBOARD.md#the-agents-claims-versus-the-read-back).
- **openIMIS claims.** On a test copy of openIMIS, the open-source insurance
  and claims system that runs Nepal's national health insurance scheme, the
  compiled program entered 149 synthetic claims with no model calls: 148 read
  back correct and none were saved wrong:
  [SCOREBOARD.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/benchmark/scoreboard/SCOREBOARD.md#openimis).

The systems each result ran on are listed in
[LIMITS.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/LIMITS.md#validated-on).

<!-- Surfaces: packages/flow/docs/SURFACES.md -->

# Execution surfaces

OpenAdapt drives six execution surfaces through one governed runtime:
`web`, `windows`, `macos`, `linux`, `rdp`, and `citrix`. The browser is one
surface among six, not a privileged default.

[BACKEND_PARITY.md](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/BACKEND_PARITY.md) lists every command and Python entry
point against the six surfaces: tested, works, or refused with its reason.

## Surface selection is explicit in production

- Under `--profile standard` or `--profile regulated`, `record` and `run`
  REFUSE to proceed without an explicit target: pass `--backend` (one of
  `web`, `windows`, `macos`, `linux`, `rdp`, `citrix`) or set `backend.kind`
  in the deployment `--config`. There is no implicit browser default in
  production.
- Under `--profile demo` (or with no profile, the permissive pre-profile
  posture), an omitted `--backend` records capture on this OS (`macos`,
  `windows`, or `linux`) and prints a visible notice. Pass `--url` without
  `--backend` to record the browser. An explicit `--backend` still wins.
  With `--profile demo`, the CLI also remembers your last explicitly
  selected target in a per-user state file
  (`~/.openadapt/flow_cli.json`, override with `OPENADAPT_FLOW_CLI_STATE`)
  and offers it as the default next time when that target is this OS, again
  with a visible notice. This convenience is CLI state only; it is never
  written into a workflow bundle.

## Workflows are bound to their surface

The recorder stamps the surface into the recording (`meta.json` `surface`),
and `compile` seals it into the bundle (`workflow.json` `surface` plus the
implied `execution_mode`). A workflow recorded and qualified on one surface
refuses to `replay`/`run` on another:

```text
run REFUSED: this workflow is bound to surface 'windows', but the resolved
backend targets 'web'. ...
```

Pass `--allow-surface-override` to proceed anyway; the override is recorded in
the run report (`surface_override: true`, alongside `recorded_surface` and
`execution_target_kind`) as compatibility evidence, so a cross-surface run is
never silent. A surface-bound bundle also supplies its own default target: an
unqualified `replay bundle` selects the bound surface rather than the browser.
Bundles compiled before surface binding carry no `surface` and behave exactly
as before.

A composition does not merge surfaces. `openadapt-flow compose` copies each
child bundle into a parent artifact; `run` executes those children one at a
time against the surface sealed into that child. There is no backend switch
inside a recording, and no parent-level `--backend` that retargets every
child.

## Execution boundary and evidence, per surface

Every substrate runs on the same small `Backend` protocol and the same governed
runtime. Each surface keeps its own deployment and evidence boundary.

| Surface | Execution boundary | Required workflow evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser (web) | Local, customer-controlled, or managed browser runner | Exact browser, application, environment, identity, effect, and policy contracts |
| Native desktop (Windows, macOS, Linux) | Local or customer-controlled | Exact host and application identity, native accessibility evidence, and an independent effect check |
| Remote display (RDP) | Local or customer-controlled | Exact client window or network session, remote-display identity, and an independent effect check |
| Citrix / VDI | Local or customer-controlled | Exact Workspace, server, application, display, identity, and effect contracts, with counted ICA/HDX trials |

Per-substrate engineering evidence is reported per the
[capability and qualification matrix](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/PRODUCT_STATUS.md):

| Substrate | Selector | Evidence basis | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web / browser | `--backend web` | Required CI and bounded field evidence | Full lifecycle on every CI build, plus third-party OpenEMR evidence |
| Native macOS (AX) | `--backend macos` | Counted task acceptance | 3/3 fixed TextEdit trials with exact file-byte effects; refused a two-window ambiguity without changing either file |
| Native Windows (UIA) | `--backend windows` | Counted task acceptance | 3/3 fixed WinForms trials with independently confirmed SQLite effects; 3/3 refusal for both stale and ambiguous targets |
| Native Linux (AT-SPI) | `--backend linux` | Required CI and counted task acceptance | Required CI drives a real GTK3 workflow through an isolated X11 / session-D-Bus environment: three verified effects, plus three ambiguous-target and three stale-target refusals |
| RDP (remote display) | `--backend rdp` | Counted task acceptance | Real-network Aardwolf RDP into Windows 11 passed 3/3 fixed remote-input trials with independent guest-tools file verification; a separate real-FreeRDP batch covers record → compile → governed replay and refusal |
| Citrix / VDI (pixel ladder) | `--backend citrix` | Required CI and counted no-DOM stand-in | Dedicated exact-Workspace-window driver, readiness gate, durable resume, and 3 healthy + 3 drift-halt no-DOM trials; the retained artifact records `ica_hdx_accepted=false` until a counted ICA/HDX run is attached |

Every row is bounded to its stated evidence. Accepted application workflows are
qualified against their own controls, session/display policy, identity evidence,
and effect oracle; code-qualified Citrix deployments additionally attach the
counted ICA/HDX record for their exact Workspace/server/application matrix.
Details:
[`backends/RDP.md`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/backends/RDP.md),
[`desktop/LINUX_NATIVE.md`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/desktop/LINUX_NATIVE.md),
[`desktop/CITRIX_PIXEL.md`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/desktop/CITRIX_PIXEL.md).

## What `record` observes

`record` opens the operator's real interface and watches what you do: real
clicks, typing, key presses, and scrolls, writing the same recording format
`compile` consumes. Perform the workflow, then press Ctrl-C (or close the
window) to finish. The `--backend` selector picks the substrate, and the same
selector is available on `replay` and `run`.

`--backend web` is browser-first (the app is a `--url`). For `windows`,
`macos`, `linux`, `rdp`, and `citrix`, the Capture component records local
screen, mouse, keyboard, timing, and available action-time structure.
`--macos-app` / `--macos-window-title` scope the macOS Capture window.
`--window` / `--window-title` scope a Windows-hosted local capture, and
`--rdp-window` / `--rdp-window-title` bind a local RDP or Citrix client window
to both capture and replay. `--task` records the operator's intent alongside
the demonstration. A compiled bundle is bound to the exact surface it was
recorded on.

`record` captures a person doing the task. An AI agent can show the task
instead, in a browser, a macOS, Linux, or native Windows app, or over RDP or
Citrix, through openadapt-agent's recording tools; see
[Recording on Windows, RDP and Citrix](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/RECORDING_ON_WINDOWS_RDP_CITRIX.md).

Install the Capture component together with the runtime for the surface that
will replay the workflow. Recorded parameter values become the defaults, and
`--param` overrides them at replay; see [`PARAMETERS.md`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/PARAMETERS.md).

## First workflow, per surface

Each surface has an equivalent record -> compile -> replay path:

| Workflow surface | Exact install |
|---|---|
| Browser | `pip install 'openadapt-flow[browser]'` |
| Native Windows | `pip install 'openadapt-flow[capture,windows]'` |
| Native macOS | `pip install 'openadapt-flow[capture,macos]'` |
| Native Linux | `pip install 'openadapt-flow[capture,linux]'` plus the AT-SPI system packages in [`desktop/LINUX_NATIVE.md`](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/desktop/LINUX_NATIVE.md) |
| Network RDP | Recorder: `pip install 'openadapt-flow[capture]'` inside the demonstrated session; runner: `pip install 'openadapt-flow[rdp]'` |
| Local RDP/Citrix client window | macOS host: `pip install 'openadapt-flow[capture,macos]'`; Windows host: `pip install 'openadapt-flow[capture,windows]'` |

```bash
# Browser (Playwright / Chromium)
openadapt-flow record --backend web --url https://your.app --out rec
openadapt-flow compile rec --out bundle --name my-task
openadapt-flow replay bundle --url https://your.app

# Attach the same recorder to one existing signed-in local Chromium tab.
openadapt-flow record --backend web --url https://your.app \
  --browser-cdp-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:9222 --out rec

# Windows: Capture records the local window; the in-guest WAA agent replays it.
openadapt-flow record --backend windows --window "Target App" --out rec
openadapt-flow compile rec --out bundle --name my-task
openadapt-flow replay bundle --agent-url http://localhost:5001

# macOS: the app and title scope the local Capture window.
openadapt-flow record --backend macos --macos-app TextEdit \
  --macos-window-title notes.txt --out rec
openadapt-flow compile rec --out bundle --name my-task
openadapt-flow replay bundle --macos-app TextEdit \
  --macos-window-title notes.txt

# Linux: Capture records the local desktop; AT-SPI selects the replay target.
openadapt-flow record --backend linux --out rec
openadapt-flow compile rec --out bundle --name my-task
openadapt-flow replay bundle --linux-app gedit \
  --linux-window-title "Untitled Document 1"

# Network RDP: run record inside the demonstrated remote session.
openadapt-flow record --backend rdp --out rec
openadapt-flow compile rec --out bundle --name my-task
openadapt-flow replay bundle --rdp-host 10.0.0.5

# Citrix / VDI (one exact local Citrix Workspace window)
openadapt-flow record --backend citrix --window "Citrix Viewer" \
  --rdp-window "Citrix Viewer" --rdp-window-title "Ward A" \
  --rdp-readiness-text "Appointments" --out rec
openadapt-flow compile rec --out bundle --name my-task
openadapt-flow replay bundle --rdp-window "Citrix Viewer" \
  --rdp-window-title "Ward A" --rdp-readiness-text "Appointments"
```

The bound surface is the replay default, so `--backend` may be omitted on
